title: SL-BiLEM: Structured Learnable Behavior-in-the-Loop Epidemic Modeling for Forecasting and Policy Evaluation

problem.claim: Epidemic forecasting must account for feedback loops caused by human behavior responding dynamically to disease spread.

gap.claim: Data-driven epidemic models become unreliable under policy-induced distribution shift.

contributions.claim: SL-BiLEM is a structured learnable behavior-in-the-loop epidemic model that uses physical constraints as regularization for robust extrapolation.

The framework decomposes effective transmission into baseline transmission and policy, media, and compliance factors, with monotonicity, smoothness, and bounded-jump constraints on learned compliance.
SL-BiLEM supports counterfactual analysis for intervention decision support in addition to epidemic forecasting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validation on three real-world datasets covering cruise-ship, school-influenza, and school-district COVID-19 surveillance forecasting.
The authors report evaluation of counterfactual recovery on synthetic benchmarks with known ground truth.

The authors report a 76% improvement over neural-mechanistic baselines, lower OOD degradation under policy-induced shift, 100% bootstrap confidence-interval coverage across 27 synthetic counterfactual experiments, and Treatment Effect Accuracy above 0.85.

narrative_sequence.summary: Human behavioral responses to disease spread create feedback loops and distribution shifts at policy intervention points.
These shifts make data-driven models unreliable.
SL-BiLEM uses physical constraints and a structured transmission decomposition to support robust extrapolation under novel policy regimes.
The framework extends beyond forecasting to counterfactual intervention analysis.
The authors report real-world forecasting validation, synthetic counterfactual evaluation, and favorable performance metrics.

source_observation.claim: The model applies monotonicity, smoothness, and bounded-jump constraints to a learned compliance function.

interpretation.claim: Domain-informed structural constraints may improve extrapolation when deployment conditions differ from training conditions.

application.claim: Use interpretable physical or behavioral constraints as regularization when building forecasting systems expected to operate across policy regimes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these constraints improve performance across other domains or policy settings.

source_observation.claim: The framework evaluates both forecasting and counterfactual recovery.

interpretation.claim: Combining predictive evaluation with counterfactual evaluation can assess both forecasting utility and intervention-analysis behavior.

application.claim: For decision-support models, evaluate predictive accuracy alongside counterfactual or intervention-related outcomes.

exception.claim: Synthetic counterfactual benchmarks may not capture all complexities of real-world intervention decisions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture or training procedure.
The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, baselines, uncertainty-calibration methodology, or statistical significance details.
The abstract does not report real-world counterfactual ground-truth validation.
